recommendations.regimenLabel: CBT and/or SSRI/SNRI after excluding organic mimics
steps: EXCLUDE organic mimics first (ACS, PE, arrhythmia, hypoglycaemia, thyrotoxicosis) — especially on first presentation.
Acute: calm reassurance, breathing techniques; benzodiazepines only sparingly/short-term if at all.
First-line ongoing treatment: CBT and/or an SSRI/SNRI.
Reduce stimulants (caffeine), alcohol; lifestyle and psychoeducation.
Arrange follow-up and safety-net; screen for depression and substance use.

drugRefs.dose: start 25 mg once daily, titrate to 50–200 mg/day
drugRefs.why: First-line drug treatment for panic disorder alongside CBT; an SNRI (e.g. venlafaxine) is an alternative. Warn of transient early worsening of anxiety.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Anxiety Disorders
NICE CG113 — Generalised Anxiety Disorder and Panic Disorder in Adults
BAP Evidence-Based Guidelines for the Pharmacological Treatment of Anxiety Disorders

drugRefs.duration: limit to a few weeks (dependence risk)
drugRefs.why: May relieve severe acute anxiety short-term, but not first-line and best avoided due to tolerance/dependence.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Anxiety Disorders
NICE CG113 — Generalised Anxiety Disorder and Panic Disorder in Adults

decision.label: CBT + SSRI; exclude organic causes first

confirm: Abrupt episodes of intense fear with somatic symptoms (palpitations, dyspnoea, chest tightness, paraesthesia) peaking within minutes — a diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out organic causes.
